title: Delayed customer notifications associated with message-broker backlog
alert_or_symptom: Customer order-confirmation and shipping-update notifications remain available but are being delivered substantially later than normal.

technical_evidence.observation: Notification delivery p95 increased from 42 seconds to 18 minutes at 06:14, while 98.7 percent of messages continued to complete successfully.
The outbound-notification queue depth increased from 1,240 to 184,600 messages, and the oldest queued message age reached 17 minutes. The broker continues to accept and persist new messages.
Delayed notification traces spend approximately 93 percent of elapsed time waiting in the Message Broker queue; Notification Service processing time remains within its normal range.
The Notification Service application instances, Application Compute Cluster and External Email and SMS Provider are healthy and operating normally.

service_impact.user_impact_description: Approximately 24 percent of order-confirmation and shipping-update messages are delivered between 12 and 20 minutes late, but messages generally arrive.
service_impact.workaround_description: Customers can view current order and shipping status in their online account.

environmental_context: The Notification Service consumes outbound notification events from the Message Broker before sending them through the External Email and SMS Provider.
The application and external communications provider remain healthy.

recent_changes.description: Routine Message Broker node maintenance completed at 05:40.

reported_unknowns: The specific producer, consumer or broker resource condition causing the queue to grow has not been identified.
The expected time required for the queue backlog to return to its normal level is not yet known.
additional_context: No messages are confirmed lost or duplicated, and no data corruption or security exposure has been observed.
